title: Direct image and finite Tor amplitude
statement:
Fix an algebraically closed field $k$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and an integer $n\geq1$. Put $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X,Y$ be finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and $f:X\to Y$ a separated finite-type morphism (separated means its diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-proper-morphism]). Use the ordinary derived categories of modules over the constant ring sheaves on the small étale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site; def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], and the module-sheaf derived direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image].

Assume a fixed integer $N\geq0$ satisfies the uniform vanishing condition, denoted here by $\operatorname{UDV}(f,A;N)$:
$$
R^rf_*M=0\quad\text{for every sheaf }M\text{ of }A_X\text{-modules and every integer }r>N.
$$
This displayed predicate is imposed for the present field $k$.

Let $a\leq b$ be integers and $K\in D^b_c(X_{\Et},A)$ a bounded constructible complex [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] with Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ [def-kun-tor-amplitude]: for every sheaf $M$ of $A_X$-modules in degree zero, $\mathcal H^i(K\otimes_A^L M)=0$ for $i\notin[a,b]$, with the ordinary étale derived tensor of [def-kun-derived-tensor]. Then $Rf_*K\in D^b_c(Y_{\Et},A)$ and $Rf_*K$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b+N]$.

proof.text: The coefficient conventions [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension] give the extended absolute value on $E$ and $\mathfrak m_E=(\varpi_E)$. By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr], $\mathcal O_E$ is a DVR with finite residue field; [lem-weil-valued-dvr-finite-quotients] therefore makes $A$ a finite local ring with maximal ideal generated by the image $\bar\varpi_E$ of $\varpi_E$. Write $\kappa=A/(\bar\varpi_E)$. The ring $A$ is Noetherian: every ideal is a finite set and hence is generated by its elements. Since the absolute value extends the $\ell$-adic one, $|\ell|_E=\ell^{-1}<1$, whence $\ell\in\mathfrak m_E=(\varpi_E)$, and $\ell^n\in(\varpi_E^n)$. Thus $\ell^n A=0$. The integer $\ell^n$ is invertible in $k$ because $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$.

source.place: Proof, fourth paragraph (finite invertible-exponent coefficients); coefficient arithmetic written explicitly.

proof.text: Put $L=K\otimes_A^L\kappa_X$. Applying the definition [def-kun-tor-amplitude] to the degree-zero sheaf $\kappa_X$ gives $\mathcal H^q(L)=0$ for $q\notin[a,b]$. In particular $L$ belongs to $D^+$ in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. To supply a bounded-below complex to the next step, take any representing complex $C$ and its good lower truncation: set $C'^i=0$ for $i<a$, $C'^a=\operatorname{coker}(d_C^{a-1})$, and $C'^i=C^i$ for $i>a$, with the induced differential. The map $C\to C'$ induces the identity on cohomology in degrees at least $a$ and an isomorphism between zero objects in lower degrees, hence is a quasi-isomorphism. Thus $C'$ represents $L$ and vanishes termwise below $a$.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph (residue-field tensor concentration); Tor amplitude: Stacks 08FZ, definition-tor-amplitude, sites-cohomology.tex.

proof.text:
By [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-grothendieck-abelian], both $\operatorname{Mod}(X_{\Et},A)$ and $\operatorname{Mod}(Y_{\Et},A)$ are Grothendieck abelian. The module direct image is additive and left exact by [lem-weil-pbc-module-direct-image-left-exact], and its derived functor is the module $Rf_*$ of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], computed by K-injectives. Apply [thm-sp-truncation-e2] to this functor and the bounded-below representative $C'$ from Step 2. Its E2-page and abutment give
$$
E_2^{p,q}=R^pf_*\mathcal H^q(L)\ \Longrightarrow\ \mathcal H^{p+q}(Rf_*L),
$$
with $E_2^{p,q}=0$ for $p<0$ and a finite exhaustive separated filtration on every abutment cohomology sheaf. All objects here are module sheaves on the small étale sites.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph; hypercohomology spectral sequence and finite filtrations: Stacks 015J, lemma-two-ss-complex-functor, derived.tex. Module categories: Stacks 03DA, 03DB, 03EW, sites-modules.tex; left exact direct image: Stacks 071J, sites-cohomology.tex.

proof.text: The page in Step 3 is supported in the rectangle $0\leq p\leq N$, $a\leq q\leq b$: the $q$-bound is Step 2, and for $p>N$ the hypothesis applies to the $A_X$-module sheaf $\mathcal H^q(L)$, without any constructibility requirement. If $t<a$ or $t>b+N$, every entry on the diagonal $p+q=t$ is zero. Each later entry is a subquotient of the preceding entry, so all $E_\infty$ entries on that diagonal are zero. The finite exhaustive separated abutment filtration supplied by [thm-sp-truncation-e2] has these entries as successive quotients. Starting at its zero end and using that every successive quotient is zero shows its whole object is zero. Consequently $\mathcal H^t(Rf_*L)=0$ for $t\notin[a,b+N]$.

source.place: Proof, third paragraph (rectangle support and vanishing of the abutment); convergence and finite filtrations: Stacks 015J, lemma-two-ss-complex-functor, derived.tex.

proof.text: Step 1 proves that $A$ is finite and annihilated by an integer $\ell^n$ invertible in $k$. The schemes $X,Y$ are finite type over the field $k$, and $K$ is bounded constructible by hypothesis. Thus [thm-dg-finite-type-constructibility] applies and gives $F:=Rf_*K\in D^b_c(Y_{\Et},A)$. This establishes the bounded constructibility clause and the hypothesis needed for the residue test below.

The sequence $A\xrightarrow{\,\bar\varpi_E\,}A\twoheadrightarrow\kappa\to0$ is a finite presentation of the $A$-module $\kappa$: the kernel of the quotient map is exactly the principal ideal generated by $\bar\varpi_E$. Also $A$ is Noetherian by Step 1, the assumed UDV is the uniform higher-direct-image vanishing required in [lem-sf-projection-finite-constant], and the bounded complex $K$ belongs to $D^-$. Applying that lemma with $M=\kappa$ yields the canonical isomorphism
$$
F\otimes_A^L\kappa_Y\ \xrightarrow{\sim}\ Rf_*(K\otimes_A^L\kappa_X)=Rf_*L.
$$
The lemma works in the ordinary unbounded étale derived categories, so the tensor with $\kappa$ is allowed even when $\kappa$ has infinite projective dimension. There is no change of direct-image functor here: the unbounded definition [def-kun-projection-formula-map] computes $Rf_*C$ as $Q(f_*I)$ for a K-injective resolution of $C$, while [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] gives the same formula for every such resolution on $D^+$. Both $K$ and $L$ belong to $D^+$, so these two computations identify the direct images of Steps 3–5 with those in the displayed projection isomorphism. Step 4 now gives $\mathcal H^t(F\otimes_A^L\kappa_Y)=0$ for $t\notin[a,b+N]$.

source.place: Proof, final paragraph (finite-presentation projection formula). Canonical map: Stacks 0B56, equation-projection-formula-map, sites-cohomology.tex; the stronger finitely-presented coefficient result is the cited DAG lemma, not an application of the perfect-coefficient lemma 0944.

proof.text: Apply [lem-exc-residue-tor-test] with $T=Y$, the actual coefficient ring $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$, its residue field $\kappa=A/(\bar\varpi_E)$, the complex $F$ of Step 5, and endpoints $a,b+N$. Its bounded constructible hypothesis holds by Step 5 and its residue-tensor vanishing condition holds by Step 6. It concludes that $F=Rf_*K$ has étale Tor amplitude in $[a,b+N]$. Together with Step 5 this proves both assertions.

source.place: Proof, final sentence (residue-field criterion); Tor-amplitude convention: Stacks 08FZ, definition-tor-amplitude, sites-cohomology.tex.
